facts: The paper 'Antibiotic-loaded cement spacers: a comprehensive review' was authored by Talha Riaz, Kathryn R. Matthias, Swathi Ramkumar, Poorani Sekar, Scott Montgomery, and Laila Woc-Colburn.
It was published on 2026-11-02 in Clinical Microbiology Reviews under DOI 10.1128/cmr.00355-25.

Two-stage exchange (TSE) is the traditional standard of care for chronic periprosthetic joint infections (PJIs), beginning with prosthesis removal and antibiotic-loaded cement spacer (ALCS) implantation.
The authors reviewed peer-reviewed literature from 1988 to 2024 along with their own clinical experience.
There is an identified lack of dosing guidance for antimicrobials in cement spacers and an absence of safety data in infectious diseases literature.

Complications associated with ALCS include persistent mechanical challenges like joint subluxation, as well as nephrotoxicity and allergic reactions from unknown levels of systemic antibiotic absorption.
The authors conclude that improved outcomes require patient-specific antimicrobial spacer dosing and a multidisciplinary team of orthopedic surgeons, infectious diseases specialists, and pharmacists.
